analysis.title: China Cosmetics: Global cosmetics read-across: Mixed 3Q26 performance in China, rising competition from LT ambition, Mainland China DFS resumed sell-in
key_insights: Mainland China growth in 3QCY26 was selective, not broad-based. Estée Lauder grew Mainland China organic sales 9% yoy (2QCY26: 7%), L'Oréal sustained MSD-HSD% sell-out growth, and P&G's SK-II grew 12% (vs 8% in 2Q). Shiseido and KOSÉ declined (Shiseido sell-out LSD% decline, KOSÉ sales -7% yoy in the cover text).

L'Oréal's China sell-out grew nearly three times the market. Management put the China cosmetics market at +2-3% for 9M26, with luxury at MSD%, dermatological slightly higher than MSD%, professional at MSD% and mass flat. Helena Rubinstein grew HDD%.

Estée Lauder gained prestige beauty share in China for a 7th consecutive quarter. 11 brands grew and 6 grew DD%, led by TOM FORD, The Ordinary, Le Labo and La Mer. Skincare and makeup grew HSD% and fragrance grew DD%.

Shiseido's China consumer purchases fell LSD% in FY3Q26, with e-commerce and offline both down LSD%. Management cited Clé de Peau Beauté and the Shiseido brand, Anessa pricing and distributor issues, non-core brand reform, a weak Hong Kong market and limited fragrance exposure.

KOSÉ's Mainland China sales grew +7.8% yoy but fell 6.6% excluding FX. Its sell-out grew at a double-digit rate, but management estimates competitors' sell-out is growing about 20% and plans corrective measures next fiscal year. KOSÉ cut FY26 net sales guidance to +3% from +6%.

Hainan is the main travel retail recovery engine. Estée Lauder reported DD% growth there, and L'Oréal, Shiseido and KOSÉ all cited positive demand or sell-out trends. Shiseido's Hainan duty-free sell-in turned positive in Q3.

Mainland China travel retail is showing early signs of recovery but remains negative at L'Oréal. L'Oréal sell-in grew about 10% against MSD% sell-out because of one-off operator inventory replenishment that is not expected to recur in 4Q. Shiseido says the mainland recovery is slower than expected.
Hainan DFS sales growth slowed to 3% yoy in 3Q26 from 5% in 2Q26, and October was down 9% yoy (Exhibit 4, Haikou Customs data).

Estée Lauder raised its FY27 outlook and expects FY1H27 growth to exceed FY2H27 because of innovation phasing and a tougher travel retail comparison base. Management says inventory is balanced and describes the FY2H27 moderation as a comparison effect, not weaker demand.

Estée Lauder's investor day (Nov 4-7, Shanghai and Hainan) set FY30 ambitions. Targets are +MSD% organic sales growth, GPM of 76%-78%, EBIT margin of 16.5%-18.5% and +DD% adj. EPS growth. It also targets 1,400 China stores by FY30 versus 1,150 in FY26 and about 30% of global innovation coming from its China Innovation Center.

P&G's China organic sales grew 8% with volume up 5%, a sixth consecutive quarter of growth. Pampers grew close to 50% on a competitor disruption and SK-II grew 12%. Olay remains an underperformer under reinvention, and management says China's mid-tier has largely disappeared.

US beauty is resilient. L'Oréal, Estée Lauder, P&G and Beiersdorf all recorded MSD% growth in CY3Q26. Dermocosmetics (La Roche-Posay, Dr.G, Aquaphor Body, The Ordinary) and social commerce (MAC's TikTok Shop, Dr.G's online-first launch) are the strongest pools.

Beiersdorf's group organic sales fell 1.3% and NIVEA fell 4.9% on trade tensions and destocking. China was a bright spot, with La Prairie net sales up 28% and sell-out in DD% growth for six quarters. Management flagged margin pressure from commodity and logistics inflation persisting in FY2H26.

Pola Orbis reported cumulative China sales of ¥4.0 billion, up 30% yoy (15% in local currency). Online growth offset store closures, while Jurlique's China sales fell on store rationalization and reduced distributor shipments.

GS's read-across is that 3Q26 results and 4Q color reinforce its view of heightened competition. Its Double 11 channel checks show domestic and international brands both stepping up consumer recruitment, launches and promotions, including aggressive MNC discounts and KOL collaborations.

GS continues to favor Mao Geping, Proya, Giant Biogene and Forest Cabin. Mao Geping is the sole Chinese brand with 4% share of China premium cosmetics, versus 82% Western, 9% Japanese and 3% Korean. Chinese and Western brands gained about 2 ppt each in 2025 versus 2021 while Korean brands lost 4 ppt.

Cost pressure is building in the supply chain. P&G raised its FY27 after-tax commodity, energy and transport headwind to US$1.4bn from US$1bn. KOSÉ expects higher Middle East raw material prices to persist next year, and Beiersdorf warned that oil sustained above US$100 could add material cost.

market_movers.rationale: Mao Geping is the sole Chinese brand with 4% share of China premium cosmetics, a differentiated position against Western brands. The target uses 21x 2027E P/E.
Proya shows strong GMV momentum in mass-market and share gain, though the 3Q26 earnings review noted a net income miss on higher brand investment. The target uses 19x 2027E P/E.
Giant Biogene has an integrated medical-aesthetics-to-skincare model, attractive valuation and Rmb7.4bn net cash as of 1H26.
Forest Cabin is favored for its oil-based skincare upcycle. The target uses 16x 2027E P/E.
Botanee's 3Q26 net income missed on lower sales and higher Double 11 selling expenses. The target uses 20x 2027E P/E.
Shanghai Jahwa's 3Q26 recurring net income beat on lower admin costs while sales lagged in non-cosmetics.
Bloomage is Sell rated with the comp sheet showing implied downside of 28% to the target.
Estée Lauder is on the conviction list. It posted 9% Mainland China organic growth, raised FY27 guidance and set FY30 targets.
Listed Buy in the comp sheet with 60% implied upside. The report gives no separate thesis.
Listed Buy in the comp sheet with 10% implied upside. The report gives no separate thesis.
L'Oréal reported 7.7% LFL organic growth and China sell-out growing nearly three times the market. Implied upside is 1%.
Beiersdorf's organic sales fell 1.3% with NIVEA down 4.9%, and margin pressure is expected to persist in FY2H26. Implied downside is 13%.
Shiseido's target history shows ¥4,300 on 10-Nov-26 versus ¥3,800 on 05-Aug-26. Management lowered FY26 LFL sales guidance but raised core OP.
KOSÉ's target history shows ¥5,000 on 10-Nov-26 versus ¥5,100 on 14-May-26. Management cut FY26 sales guidance to +3% from +6%, and implied downside is 19%.
Amorepacific is listed Buy with 40% implied upside in the comp sheet.
Pola Orbis kept FY26 sales and operating profit guidance and raised recurring and net profit forecasts on FX gains.
Cosmax is Neutral rated in the comp sheet with 25% implied downside.

sector_views.rationale: GS likes Mao Geping, Proya, Giant Biogene and Forest Cabin despite heightened competition and promotions from Western brands.
Korean brands lost 4 ppt of China premium share in 2025 versus 2021. KOSÉ is rated Sell and Shiseido and KOSÉ saw China sell-out declines or lagged competitors in 3Q.
Hainan is the clear recovery engine, but DFS growth slowed to 3% yoy in 3Q26 from 5% in 2Q and October fell 9% yoy.
US beauty is broadly resilient at MSD% growth, with dermocosmetics, accessible premiumization and social commerce the strongest growth pools.

earnings_insights: L'Oréal FY3Q26 (reported): organic sales +7.7% LFL, with Dermatological Beauty and Professional Products both +13.9%. Regions: SAPMENA +19.5%, Europe +8.9%, North America +5.6%, North Asia +7.8%.

Estée Lauder F1Q27 (CY3Q26, reported): organic sales +6%, APAC +10%, Mainland China +9%, Americas and EUKEM +4%. Company guidance for FY27: organic sales +4.0%-5.5%, adj. EBIT margin 12.9%-13.7%, adj. EPS US$3.20-US$3.45, raised to reflect FQ1 upside. FY1H27 growth is expected to exceed FY2H27.

P&G FY1Q27 (CY3Q26, reported): organic sales +4% (flat in FY4Q26), Beauty +5.4%, China +8% organic and +5% volume, US +3%. Company guidance reiterated: FY27 organic sales +1-3% and core EPS flat to +3%. After-tax commodity, energy and transport headwinds were raised to US$1.4bn from US$1bn, and the net sales outlook was raised for the Thorne acquisition.

Shiseido FY3Q26 (reported): net sales +3% LFL, with Japan flat, China/Travel Retail +5%, Asia Pacific +7%, Americas +4% and EMEA flat. Management lowered its FY26 LFL net sales forecast and raised core OP on profitability and FX. About JPY5.5 billion of marketing was deferred from Q3 to Q4.
KOSÉ FY3Q26 (reported): net sales +5.7% yoy, with high prestige +9.3% and prestige +13.2%. FY26 net sales guidance was lowered to +3% from +6%, with prestige growth now forecast at -LSD%.

Pola Orbis FY3Q26 (reported): sales +1.3% yoy, Orbis +5.0%, Pola -0.6% with salon -6.0%. Guidance for sales and operating profit was unchanged, and recurring and net profit forecasts were raised on FX gains.

Beiersdorf FY26Q3 (reported): organic sales -1.3%, Consumer -0.7%, NIVEA -4.9%, La Prairie net sales +28%. FY26 guidance is a LSD% decline in Consumer organic sales with EBIT margin of at least 11%, and tesa EBIT margin now carries risk from the semiconductor shortage.

Domestic China names (3Q26 results, reported, per the More Reads headlines): Proya net income missed on greater brand investment, Botanee net income missed on lower sales and higher Double 11 selling expenses, and Shanghai Jahwa's recurring net income beat on lower admin costs.

trade_ideas.description: Preference for Mao Geping, Proya, Giant Biogene and Forest Cabin within China cosmetics, all Buy rated with 12-month targets
trade_ideas.rationale: GS continues to like Mao Geping for its differentiated brand positioning, Proya for mass-market share gain, Giant for its integrated model and net cash, and Forest Cabin for its oil-based skincare upcycle.
trade_ideas.risk: More intense-than-expected competition and promotions, including tougher competition with overseas premium brands.

risk_factors: More intense competition and promotional activity in China, including aggressive MNC discounts and KOL collaborations during Double 11.

Sell-in running ahead of sell-out in travel retail (L'Oréal, Shiseido, KOSÉ), with the one-off L'Oréal replenishment not expected to recur in 4Q and inventory adjustments possible if balance is not reached by year-end.
Hainan DFS growth is slowing, with October down 9% yoy.
Tougher travel retail comparison base for Estée Lauder in FY2H27.
Higher commodity, energy, transport and raw material costs (P&G US$1.4bn headwind, KOSÉ, Beiersdorf), with oil above US$100 flagged as a risk.
Shiseido's China recovery depends on structural reform, Anessa inventory normalization and a weak Hong Kong market.
Company-specific risks listed for GS targets include slower product development at Proya, slower skincare expansion at Mao Geping, and over-concentration in essence oil at Forest Cabin.
charts_described: Exhibit 4 plots Hainan DFS monthly sales yoy from Jan-25 to Oct-26, with growth of 3% yoy in 3Q26 vs 5% in 2Q26 and October at a 9% yoy decline (Haikou Customs).
Exhibit 5 shows China's premium beauty market mix by brand origin from 2014 to 2025, described as 96%+ dominated by global players, or c.80% by Western players (Euromonitor).
geopolitical: Middle East supply-chain disruptions have raised logistics costs for Beiersdorf, and KOSÉ expects higher Middle East raw material prices to continue into next fiscal year.
Beiersdorf said prior US tariff payments had been refunded and ongoing tariffs remain manageable given its US and Mexico production footprint.
Chinese inbound travel to Japan remains subdued, so KOSÉ is prioritizing promotions in Hainan, Hong Kong, Thailand and other destinations.

tension_points.bull_case: Western MNCs are outgrowing a LSD% to MSD% market. Estée Lauder grew Mainland China organic sales 9% and gained prestige share for a 7th quarter, L'Oréal's sell-out grew nearly three times the market, and P&G's SK-II grew 12%.
tension_points.bear_case: Shiseido and KOSÉ lost ground, with KOSÉ's China sell-out growing below competitors' estimated 20%. GS's channel checks show rising promotions and deep MNC discounts into Double 11, and Shiseido cited weak Hong Kong and Anessa distributor issues.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management at KOSÉ and Shiseido expects sell-in and sell-out to balance by year-end, so continued sell-in running ahead of sell-out would revive the inventory-adjustment concern.

tension_points.bull_case: Hainan is the clear recovery engine with Estée Lauder at DD% growth. Mainland China travel retail is narrowing its decline after airport transitions, and L'Oréal expects its travel retail sell-out to turn positive in FY4Q26.
tension_points.bear_case: Hainan DFS growth slowed to 3% in 3Q26 from 5% and October fell 9% yoy. L'Oréal's 3Q sell-in uplift was one-off inventory replenishment, and Shiseido says the mainland recovery is slower than expected.
tension_points.what_invalidates: L'Oréal's expectation that its travel retail sell-out turns positive in FY4Q26 failing to materialize.
